          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We  heard  Mr.  Amit  Sibal,  the  learned  senior  counsel
appearing for the petitioner, and Mr. Jayant Mehta, the learned
senior counsel appearing for the respondent nos. 1, 2 and 3
respectively. 
2. This petition arises from the judgment and order passed by
the Division Bench of the High Court of Delhi dated 27.02.2026
in  FAO(OS)(COMM)  No.  111/2024  by  which  the  First  Appeal
preferred by the petitioner against the judgment passed by a
learned Single Judge of the High Court dated 15.05.2024 came to
be dismissed.
3. Mr. Sibal would submit that the respondents Trade mark
“Baby Forest” is similar to the trade mark of the petitioner
namely “Forest Essentials” and “Forest Essentials Baby”.
4. According to him, these are identical Baby products.  He
would submit that the petitioner adopted its trade mark sometime
in 2001, and at the time of adoption of similar marks by the
respondents,  the annual sales and marketing expenses were over
428 crores and 32 crore, respectively, whereas the respondents
sales were around 2 crore. 
5. We are further informed that the infringement suit(s)
2

## Page 461

SLP(C)  No.13183/2026
instituted by the petitioner is liable to be stayed under
Section  124  of  the  Trade  Marks  Act  as  the  Rectification
Petitions are pending before the High Court.
6. In other words, the challenge by the petitioner is to the
registration of the Trade Mark of the respondents in the name
“Baby Forest”.
7. We are of the view that the petitioner should pursue
further with these C.O.(COMM.IPDTM) Nos.186-191 of 2023 before
the High Court.
8. We are informed that the Rectification Petitions are coming
up for hearing on 21.08.2026.
9. We believe after hearing both the sides that it will be in
the fitness of things if the High Court gives some priority and
decides all the Rectification Petitions and disposed them of in
accordance with law without being influenced in any manner by
any of the observations made in the impugned judgment passed by
the Division Bench of the Delhi High Court including the
judgment of the learned Single Judge.
10. All questions of law are kept open to be agitated before
the Court concerned.
11. With the aforesaid, this Special Leave Petition is disposed
of.

1. Hon’ble Mr.Justice Sanjay Karol pronounced a reportable
judgment of the Bench comprising His Lordship and Hon’ble
Mr.Justice Nongmeikapam Kotiswar Singh.
2. The appeal is allowed in terms of signed reportable
judgment.
3. The relevant paragraphs of the judgment are extracted as
under:
“18. However,  insofar  as  the  amount  of
penalty  imposed  under  section  15G  is
concerned, taking a cumulative view of the
facts and circumstances of the present case
as already discussed above, we are of the
view  that  Rs.25  Lakhs  as  penalty  to
Respondent  No.1  may  be  excessive.
Accordingly, the same is reduced to 10 Lakhs
i.e., the minimum penalty as imposed on
Respondent Nos. 2 and 3. 

## Page 642

19. Before parting with the matter, we may
observe that in the impugned judgment, the
SAT  appears  to  recognize  a  defense  to
insider trading, i.e., legitimate corporate
purpose as was interpreted by the SAT in
Rakesh Agrawal v. Securities Exchange Board
of India1, which was a decision rendered in
the context of the 1992 PIT Regulations.
That, however, was not a course open for
the SAT to take in the impugned judgment in
view of the note appended in Regulation
4(1).
20. The penalty is modified to the above
extent.  The same shall be paid within a
period  of  three  months,  if  not  already
paid.”
3. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner  before this  Court has  filed the
present petition, being aggrieved by the impugned order
dated  23.06.2026  passed  by  the  High  Court  of  Madhya
Pradesh, Jabalpur in WP No. 12811 of 2026.
2. The facts of the case reveal that this Court had
directed the State of Madhya Pradesh for removal of all
encroachments in the matter, however, on one pretext or the
other, the persons like petitioner are not permitting the
1

## Page 680

State  Government  to  take  steps  for  removal  of
encroachments.
3. In the main petition which was listed recently,
i.e., SLP (C) No. 29145/2018, a miscellaneous application
was filed and this Court has again directed the State
Government to ensure that the encroachments are removed.
4. It is unfortunate that the orders passed by this
Court  are  not  being  complied  with,  and  in  order  to
circumvent the orders passed by this Court, such petitions
are being filed.
5. The State authorities are directed to ensure that
the orders passed by this Court are complied with.
6. With  the  above  observation,  the  Special  Leave
Petition stands dismissed.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

in  accordance  with  lease  even  before  expiry  of
aforesaid lease period.

is dismissed.
v. in the peculiar facts of the case, the parties
shall bear their respective expenses.”

open for the Corporation to take steps, including action of
termination of lease in accordance with lease agreement even
before the expiry of the lease period.

to proceed further in accordance with law.

has been offered by the petitioners.

of delay as well as on merits.

1. Before we proceed further on this petition, we
deem  it  appropriate  to  ascertain  whether  the
petitioner-company had, at any stage, questioned the
order  passed  by  the  learned  Magistrate  dated
14.10.2014 either before the High Court or before
the Sessions Court.

invited our attention to Annexure P-17 which is an
order purportedly passed on a complaint filed by
Yash Papers Limited. We fail to understand how Yash
Papers Limited would be able to maintain a complaint
under the provisions of the Protection of Women from
Domestic Violence Act, 2005.
3. In such circumstances, the learned counsel for
the petitioner shall file an additional affidavit
bringing on record true and correct copies of the
documents and also disclosing whether the petitioner
had taken recourse to any proceedings either before
the High Court or before the Sessions Court against
the  order  of  the  learned  Magistrate  dated
14.10.2014.

granted.

prosecution intends to examine 36 witnesses.

disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The appeal is directed against the interim order dated 14 th October, 2015
of the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench.  The operative
portion of the impugned order reads as follows:
“...Accordingly, operation of the order dated 11.9.2015
is stayed and the opposite parties are directed to allow
the petitioner to work in pursuance to the appointment
letter, which has been issued, provided the same has not
been cancelled as alleged by the petitioner’s counsel.”
2. It is the categorical case of the appellants before us that the respondent
has not been issued any appointment letter.

## Page 976

2
3. If indeed that be so, there was no question of the Union of India feeling
aggrieved and carrying the impugned interim order in appeal before us.
4. Be  that  as  it  may,  having  heard  Ms.  Archana  Pathak  Dave,  learned
Additional Solicitor General appearing for the appellants and Mr. Pradeep Kant,
learned senior counsel appearing for the respondent, we require Mr. Kant to
place  before  us  the  appointment  letter  allegedly  issued  in  favour  of  the
respondent by the appellants.
5. Re-list the civil appeal after two weeks.
(JATINDER KAUR)                              (SUDHIR KUMAR SHARMA)

investigation has been completed, and charge-sheet has been filed.
It was further submitted that the Postmortem Report recorded no
injuries on the body of the deceased, except for the ligature mark
on the neck resulting from the suicide. 
6. On a prima facie consideration of the material on record and
after hearing the learned counsel for the parties, we are of the
opinion that the petitioner can be released on bail, subject to the
terms and conditions that the  Additional Sessions Judge/Special
Judge, Chandrapur, Maharashtra (the jurisdictional Court) may deem
fit and appropriate to impose. 
7. Ordered accordingly.
8. The petitioner shall appear before the  Additional Sessions
Judge/Special Judge, Chandrapur, Maharashtra as and when directed
and cooperate with the trial.
9. With the above directions, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)
